html:
SMTO-SKL-0114 — Too many Slack sign-ins are waiting to be finished

GUID: 4a5d6b1f-2878-54eb-b3e6-3058cd34ede5
Slug: slack-oauth-too-many-pending
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • SMTO can keep up to 32 unfinished Slack sign-in links at once, and that limit is reached, so no new link was made. Unfinished links expire after 10 minutes. No Slack connection was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you already have a Slack sign-in page open from SMTO, finish it in that browser tab. Each finished sign-in frees a place for a new one.
  2. Otherwise, wait 10 minutes before asking SMTO to connect Slack again. Unfinished links expire after 10 minutes and are then removed from the waiting list.
  3. If you didn't start these sign-ins, look for a Task or Schedule that keeps asking to connect Slack, and stop it. A Task that asks for a connection over and over can fill every place on its own.
  4. Then ask SMTO to connect Slack once, and finish that sign-in before starting another. Handling one sign-in at a time keeps you under the limit.

What success looks like

  • SMTO gives you a new Slack sign-in link, and finishing it shows the Connected page.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO; sign-ins started by other people using the same SMTO count toward this limit too. Don't keep requesting new links, because each request adds to the queue.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • BrowserOAuth.start refused a new Slack authorization because 32 unexpired pending handshakes already exist for the Slack provider after expired ones were removed.

What this means

  • Shared OAuth start finds its maximum number of live pending authorization transactions already present. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Shared OAuth start finds its maximum number of live pending authorization transactions already present.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect existing pending flows and their expiry.

How to fix it

  • Complete existing handshakes or let them expire (600 seconds each; they live only in Server memory and are also discarded on Server restart, which invalidates every outstanding link). Look for a Task or Schedule looping on slack.connect, stop it, then start a single new consent.
  • Complete or wait for existing consent requests to expire before starting another.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing flows complete or expire before another request is admitted.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
